description: Welcome to Chronos Earth. I am a full-stack developer specializing in Python, JavaScript, and React architectures. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I am building an advanced web app to process NASA Earth science datasets, generate time-series visualizations, and analyze environmental trends dynamically, bridging complex scientific data with intuitive user interaction.
summary: Chronos Earth is an interactive web platform developed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Relying solely on global climate averages masks critical regional anomalies. To address this, we developed a tool that democratizes Earth-science data by allowing users to select specific geographic regions, pull NASA datasets, and generate multi-decade time-series visualizations. Crucially, it goes beyond simple visuals by computing robust statistical metrics—including Mann-Kendall tests and Sen's Slope—to prove whether an observed regional trend is mathematically significant. This project is important because it translates complex scientific and statistical data into plain-language summaries. By doing so, it prevents causal overclaiming and empowers students and citizens to become genuine environmental detectives, fostering true climate literacy without requiring a data science background.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Chronos Earth is an interactive "Earth System Trend Detective" web platform. It allows users to discover Earth-science variables (e.g., precipitation, surface temperature) and select a regional bounding box to analyze environmental anomalies over time. Behind the scenes, the platform's logic spatially aggregates gridded NASA data and runs an automated statistical analysis. Instead of relying on potentially deceptive visual "trend lines," it computes non-parametric Mann-Kendall tests (for monotonic trends) and Sen’s slope estimation (for the rate of change), yielding clear p-values and confidence intervals.

Benefits & Intended Impact: While climate change is a global issue, its impacts are deeply regional. The primary benefit of Chronos Earth is that it translates complex scientific and statistical data into plain-language summaries. By explicitly warning users against causal overclaiming (e.g., reminding them that statistical significance implies a dataset trend, not immediate attribution to a specific cause), we intend to build true, reproducible climate literacy. It empowers students, educators, and citizens to become genuine environmental detectives without requiring a data science background.

Tools, Languages, & Software Used: We developed a responsive web application hosted and deployed via Base44. The frontend was built using modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) to ensure an accessible, dark-themed cyber-detective UI. For our data architecture, we integrated conceptual API workflows targeting NASA's Earth Observing System Data and Information System (EOSDIS), specifically structuring queries for NASA Giovanni and GES DISC datasets (such as GPM, MODIS, and GLDAS).

Creativity & Factors Considered: Most climate dashboards stop at drawing a chart. Our creative approach was to tackle the mathematics and scientific integrity. We closely considered the risk of "Visual Bias"—the danger that a user sees a rising line on a graph and falsely assumes absolute scientific proof. By enforcing statistical rigor (handling missing values, calculating p-values) and pairing it with plain-language text, we successfully bridged the gap between raw NASA Earth data and public comprehension.
